Commentary.Commentary: We are back with Sri Lanka's reply in their second inning! The umpires are out and are followed closely by the England team who spread out to take the field. Nishan Madushka and Dimuth Karunaratne are the openers for Sri Lanka who are marking their guards. Chris Woakes is handed the new ball and will start the proceedings for England. Here we go..
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Right then, with the game finely poised it will be fascinating to see how Sri Lanka approaches their second innings. Can they dig out a big second innings lead, or will the English bowlers rise to the challenge once again? The stage is set for a riveting third innings, where every run and wicket will shape the narrative of this encounter.

On the other hand, the Lankan bowlers began their innings on a promising note, claiming 4 wickets for just 125 runs. However, as the game progressed, things started to unravel for them. They struggled to find breakthroughs, and even when they managed to take a wicket, they couldn't capitalize on it. A much-needed respite finally came late in the day when they broke the partnership between Atkinson and Smith, triggering a mini-collapse. From there, they were able to take successive wickets, eventually bundling England out for 358 runs.

England have set themselves up for success in the first innings, securing a substantial lead of 122 runs. A series of small but crucial partnerships have propelled the Three Lions forward, with special credit due to the middle order. Notably, Root, Brook, and Smith contributed significantly, turning the tide in England's favour. Jamie Smith deserves particular praise for his maiden century, a well-crafted 111 runs off 148 deliveries. The lower order also played a vital role, adding valuable runs to ensuring England firmly hold the upper hand at the close of the innings.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! England have breached the 300-run mark and they currently hold a narrow lead of 69 runs. Sure, the first 45 minutes or so, belonged to England as the Sri Lankan bowlers looked very unsettled and we saw too many bowling changes. The ball drifted degrees due to that gusty wind blowing across Old Trafford, but the English batters looked highly accommodated to the movement of the ball. Jamie Smith and Gus Atkinson stitched a solid 66-run stand with Smith comfortably notching up his maiden Test century. But, England lost Gus Atkinson right before the break. England will be looking to rebuild again, as they do not have a comfortable lead currently, but will feel relaxed as Smith is still unbeaten on 101. Sri Lanka on the other hand will aim to take consecutive breakthroughs. Well then, Matthew Potts is the new batter in at number 9 for England.

Commentary.Commentary: In all readiness to start the day's play! To make up for the lost overs, the first two sessions will include a 15-minute extension and an additional 30 minutes will be added at the end of the day to bowl the designated 98 overs. The weather forecast for the day looks more promising, despite the presence of heavy cloud cover and a slight chance of light showers early on. Fortunately, interruptions are expected to be minimal as the day progresses, and we're hopeful for a full day's play. With the match finely balanced, today could be pivotal, and by the end of it, weather permitting, we should have a much clearer picture of which direction this Test match is heading. So, brace yourself for another thrilling day of cricket that is just around the corner!

On the other hand, the Sri Lankan bowlers and fielders will come into Day 3 rejuvenated after enduring a long and grueling day in the field. Despite the challenges, they've done remarkably well to maintain their discipline, preventing England from running away with the game. As the spinners look to play a more decisive role, Dhananjaya de Silva will be hoping his bowlers can quickly dismantle the remaining four wickets, allowing Sri Lanka to get back to the crease and make amends for their modest first-innings performance.

England will be pleased to have erased the deficit and secured a narrow 24-run lead by the close of Day 2. Just as things seemed to be going smoothly for them, the day was unfortunately cut short by bad light and weather, reminiscent of the interruptions on Day 1. Jamie Smith remains at the crease, intent on building England's advantage, with the tail-enders playing a vital role in adding crucial runs. Don’t be surprised if England adopts an aggressive approach today to pile up runs quickly and put Sri Lanka under the pump.

Hello and a warm welcome to the third day's play of this gripping first Test match between England and Sri Lanka at Emirates Old Trafford in Manchester. With the game perfectly balanced, we're set for an exciting day of red-ball cricket that could prove decisive, living up to the anticipation of the so-called 'Moving Day'. Be certain to expect a day full of twists, turns, and immersive cricket as both teams strive to gain the upper hand.
… DAY 3, SESSION 1 …

Right then, with the game finely poised, Day 3 could very well be the turning point of this Test match, determining the direction it will take. England will look to add crucial runs to their total, while Sri Lanka will be eager to return fresh and work through to get rid of the remaining 4 wickets as quickly as possible. The pivotal 'Moving Day' action kicks off on Friday, 23 August at 10 am GMT, but be sure to join us earlier for all the build-up. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

Earlier in the second session of the day, the momentum shifted back and forth, leaving the game finely poised with England at 176/4. Harry Brook and Jamie Smith were well set at the crease, with England trailing by just 60 runs at the end of the session. Asitha Fernando bowled brilliantly for the visitors, claiming three crucial wickets early on, despite stabilizing contributions from Dan Lawrence and Joe Root. However, Brook and Smith took advantage of the tiring Sri Lankan bowlers, steadily rotating the strike and finding the occasional boundary to keep the scoreboard ticking.

Prabath Jayasuriya provided a crucial breakthrough early in the session, dismissing Harry Brook with a brilliant delivery that gripped and turned, a much-needed wicket given how well Brook was playing, breaking the 62-run stand. Chris Woakes then joined Jamie Smith at the crease, and the pair capitalized on the weary Sri Lankan bowlers, forging another valuable 52-run partnership that pushed England past the deficit. However, Prabath Jayasuriya struck again with a nearly identical delivery, removing Woakes and relieving some pressure on the visitors before bad light and rain returned bringing the day's play to a halt.

Despite losing an entire session to rain earlier, the remainder of the day provided some captivating cricket until the conditions became too gloomy and dark, forcing the players off the field. England have managed to erase the deficit and now hold a lead of 23 runs with 4 wickets still in hand, and Jamie Smith well set at 72 off 97 balls.

As we head into the final session, England trails by just 60 runs, with Brook and Smith well set at the crease. Expect a fascinating contest as Sri Lanka will be eager to break this partnership and keep the lead manageable, while England will look to build on their momentum and edge closer to Sri Lanka’s total. The final session promises to be an intriguing battle, don’t miss it. The start of the final session is at 3.20 pm GMT. Do join us then.

However, a gritty 27-run stand between Joe Root and Dan Lawrence helped stabilize the innings, and Root then found solid support from Harry Brook. Together, they added a crucial 58 runs for the fourth wicket, showing a calculated approach against some sharp bowling. As the session progressed, Sri Lanka’s bowlers began to tire, and Brook, along with Jamie Smith, took advantage, comfortably rotating the strike and keeping the scoreboard ticking.

We’ve reached the Tea break on Day 2, and what a session it’s been! The rain may have delayed the start, but once play resumed, it was Sri Lanka who made the early breakthroughs, with Asitha Fernando striking twice in quick succession, by getting the better of Ben Duckett and Ollie Pope, putting Sri Lanka firmly in the driver's seat.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! Both Asitha Fernando and Vishwa Fernando’s exceptional bowling has reinvigorated Sri Lanka’s position in the game. The consistent line and length have earned the visitors three crucial wickets, and they will be eager to capitalize on this momentum. England, struggling to form partnerships, will now look to their new pair at the crease to stabilize the innings. With challenging overhead conditions and precise bowling from the opposition, it’s crucial for the English batters to weather the storm and regain control. Day 1 was nothing short of a rollercoaster, with England’s bowlers making the most of the early conditions to have Sri Lanka in all sorts of trouble.
